Lord Byron, Don Juan, edited by Ernest Hertley Coleridge.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/lord-byron/don-juan

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Lord Byron, the author, died 1824.
- Ernest Hertley Coleridge, the editor, died 1920 (the Standard Ebooks credit spells the name Hertley; Wikipedia spells it Hartley).

First publication of the text used: 1824 (SE colophon: 'Don Juan was published in 1824 by Lord Byron.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1824, before 1931; a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1919.
- Country of origin (the facts do not name the country of first publication): the last person to die did so in 1920. The text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, from 1 January 2021.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Don Juan was published in 1824 by Lord Byron.'
- Wikidata Q5679 (Lord Byron), P570 = 1824-04-19
- Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_Hartley_Coleridge: died February 1920 at Aylesbury
